fields_of_interest.message:
Before you blindly pay a medical bill, READ THE BILL.

Medical billing is one of those areas where a lot of people assume the number printed at the bottom is just the number they owe.

Sometimes it is.

Sometimes there are duplicate charges, coding mistakes, services you don’t recognize, or discounts that were never applied.

That’s why asking for an itemized bill is such a basic move, but a surprisingly important one. You want to know exactly what you’re being charged for before handing over thousands of dollars.

And if the bill is still crushing you, call the billing department. Ask questions. Ask if there’s a cash-pay discount. Ask about financial assistance. Ask if there’s any adjustment available.

Worst case, they say no.

Best case, one phone call saves you hundreds or even thousands.

Medical bills are expensive enough without paying for stuff you shouldn’t be paying for in the first place.

Every missed filing deadline is lost revenue submit clean claims on time and protect every dollar your practice earns.
